<reflection>
The second experiment introduced initial product and higher catalyst concentration. The fitting results show that mechanisms M19 and M9 have the best fits, but many others remain plausible with negative log-likelihood values within a narrow range. This indicates that while product and catalyst variations provided some discrimination, substantial uncertainty persists across multiple deactivation and dimerization mechanisms. The aim of the second experiment was partially achieved, but further data is needed to distinguish among the crowded set of candidates.
</reflection>
<hypothesis>
I propose an experiment with low substrate (0.5 M), high catalyst (0.15 M), and no initial product. This condition targets catalyst-dependent phenomena: high catalyst concentration amplifies effects of dimerization (M2, M3) and catalyst-involved deactivation pathways (e.g., M9, M13, M19), while low substrate avoids saturation and makes the system sensitive to catalyst availability. The absence of product isolates substrate-catalyst interactions, complementing the previous run with product. This design should help differentiate between deactivation mechanisms that depend solely on catalyst (M9) versus those requiring catalyst-substrate complexes (M19), and also stress dimerization equilibria, providing broad discrimination across the plausible set.
</hypothesis>
